passages.text: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of David. After Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.”
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He wrote it as a Maskil, which is a type of instructive song.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
Doeg was an Edomite.
Doeg went to Saul.
Doeg told Saul, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.”

passages.text: Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man? The loving devotion of God endures all day long.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He wrote it for the choirmaster.
Doeg the Edomite went to Saul.
Doeg told Saul, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.”
David spoke to a powerful man who did evil.
He said, “Why do you boast about evil, mighty man?”
God’s loving devotion lasts all day.
God’s kindness never ends.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִֽד׃ בְּב֤וֹא׀ דּוֹאֵ֣ג הָאֲדֹמִי֮ וַיַּגֵּ֪ד לְשָׁ֫א֥וּל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֑וֹ בָּ֥א דָ֝וִ֗ד אֶל־ בֵּ֥ית אֲחִימֶֽלֶךְ׃ מַה־ תִּתְהַלֵּ֣ל בְּ֭רָעָה הַגִּבּ֑וֹר חֶ֥סֶד אֵ֝֗ל כָּל־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to Doeg the Edomite.
Doeg told Saul that David went to the house of Ahimelech.
David calls Doeg a worker of deceit.
David says, "Your tongue plans destruction."
Your tongue is like a sharp razor.
You use your words to deceive.
passages.original: הַ֭וּוֹת תַּחְשֹׁ֣ב לְשׁוֹנֶ֑ךָ כְּתַ֥עַר מְ֝לֻטָּ֗שׁ עֹשֵׂ֥ה רְמִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking truth. Selah You love every word that devours, O deceitful tongue.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to a deceitful man.
This man loves evil more than good.
He prefers lies over speaking the truth.
He loves every word that destroys.
His tongue is full of deceit.
Selah.
passages.original: אָהַ֣בְתָּ רָּ֣ע מִטּ֑וֹב שֶׁ֓קֶר׀ מִדַּבֵּ֖ר צֶ֣דֶק סֶֽלָה׃ אָהַ֥בְתָּ כָֽל־ דִּבְרֵי־ בָ֗לַע לְשׁ֣וֹן מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah The righteous will see and fear; they will mock the evildoer, saying, “Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and strengthened himself by destruction.”
passages.sermon:
God will act against the evildoer.
God will bring you down to everlasting ruin.
God will snatch you up.
God will tear you away from your tent.
God will uproot you from the land of the living.
The righteous will see this.
The righteous will fear.
The righteous will mock the evildoer.
They will say, “Look at this man.
He did not make God his refuge.
He trusted in the abundance of his wealth.
He found strength in his own destruction.”
passages.original: גַּם־ אֵל֮ יִתָּצְךָ֪ לָ֫נֶ֥צַח יַחְתְּךָ֣ וְיִסָּחֲךָ֣ מֵאֹ֑הֶל וְשֵֽׁרֶשְׁךָ֨ מֵאֶ֖רֶץ חַיִּ֣ים סֶֽלָה׃ וְיִרְא֖וּ צַדִּיקִ֥ים וְיִירָ֗אוּ וְעָלָ֥יו יִשְׂחָֽקוּ׃ הִנֵּ֤ה הַגֶּ֗בֶר לֹ֤א יָשִׂ֥ים אֱלֹהִ֗ים מָֽע֫וּזּ֥וֹ וַ֭יִּבְטַח בְּרֹ֣ב עָשְׁר֑וֹ יָ֝עֹ֗ז בְּהַוָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever.
passages.sermon:
I am like an olive tree.
I am flourishing.
I am in the house of God.
I trust in God's loving devotion.
I trust God forever.
I trust God always.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י׀ כְּזַ֣יִת רַ֭עֲנָן בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּטַ֥חְתִּי בְחֶֽסֶד־ אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים עוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

passages.text: I will praise You forever, because You have done it. I will wait on Your name— for it is good— in the presence of Your saints.
passages.sermon:
I will praise You forever.
You have done it.
I will wait for Your name.
Your name is good.
I will do this in the presence of Your saints.
passages.original: אוֹדְךָ֣ לְ֭עוֹלָם כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֑יתָ וַאֲקַוֶּ֖ה שִׁמְךָ֥ כִֽי־ ט֝֗וֹב נֶ֣גֶד חֲסִידֶֽיךָ׃
